findings.title: An added contradictory MPN field escapes identity audit and real schematic parity

evidence.controls: Changing canonical Manufacturer Part instead produces one genuine footprint_symbol_field_mismatch parity warning; exact native SaveBoard control equals original SHA and has 0/0/0.
evidence.current_board: No alternate MPN/Part Number fields found in the actual board; canonical metadata/parity are clean.

source.basis: Maker ordering format uses R as decimal point for these resistance codes; 2R00 and 20R0 name different resistances.

evidence.broader_catches: Original fab manifest rejects changed CAD. Recomputed native power budget differs in fire_current_GAP1 board provenance. No whole-gate escape was executed or claimed.

findings.fix: Extend the existing metadata field walk to normalize known MPN/part-number aliases and reject conflicting second identities; retain canonical LCSC/Manufacturer/Manufacturer Part and parity checks. Seed both a conflicting extra MPN and a valid matching alias, or prohibit redundant MPN aliases explicitly.

findings.title: S-4 accepts the same required designator in two different production BOM rows

evidence.seed: Append a second Qty=1 R134 row with Manufacturer Part CRM2512-FX-20R0ELF and LCSC Part # C0; keep every genuine original row and the current native PCB/schematic/CPL.
evidence.controls: Current 82-row/199-part BOM passes. Existing positive-Qty and per-row distinct-count checks are retained; the new gap is reference reuse across rows.
evidence.current_board: Actual BOM designators are unique and quantities correct.

source.basis: R134 identity in the two seeded rows is contradictory by the maker ordering code; uniqueness itself is the native one-footprint/one-designator assembly contract, not a maker electrical threshold.

evidence.broader_catches: The original five-output manifest rejects the altered BOM. Exporter regeneration from unique board references prevents this edit in the present exporter. A faulty future exporter with newly matching manifest was not executed.

findings.fix: Track the first row for each designator in assembly_population and reject a designator appearing in any second row, including a conflicting code/MPN. Preserve the current distinct-within-row rule and quantity-free CPL behavior.

findings.title: Paste checker ignores actual aperture geometry

evidence.seed: In an isolated copy of the actual F_Paste Gerber, change only %ADD28R,0.566000X0.540000*% to %ADD28R,0.001000X0.001000*%; repackage with every other Gerber byte unchanged.
evidence.controls: Unmodified package also passes. Both live layer-data check and the repacked zip check accept the tiny apertures; coordinates and component identifiers are untouched.
evidence.current_board: The actual package retains the full 0.566x0.540 mm rectangular aperture, matching these native pads; no current paste defect is demonstrated.

source.basis: Primary supplier identifies R127 C11702 as UNI-ROYAL 0402WGF1001TCE, 1kOhm 0402. The measured paste requirement here is the existing native pad/paste geometry, not an invented maker stencil floor; almost-zero solder coverage is a prospective manufacturing inference.

evidence.broader_catches: The unchanged manifest rejects the changed Gerber zip. No reissued manifest/faulty exporter whole-gate escape or physical soldering result is claimed.

findings.fix: Read ADD aperture/macro definitions and compare exported geometry/area with native expected paste polygons. Ordinary lead apertures follow their reviewed native paste margins; exposed pads retain maker-approved window/segmentation patterns, and explicitly reviewed manual-after-reflow process exceptions remain scoped. Use the existing expected native area/pattern semantics, or a maker/process-sourced bound when needed; add no universal copper-coverage percentage or solder-volume claim. Fail closed for unsupported geometry; retain flash-count, position and dry-pad checks. Add under/oversize and valid equivalent/window/manual-exception controls.
